name: Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI)
source: Five level near-side frames (frames 2-6 at 4 fps from t=17.0 s) from Hammer Strength's official Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI) demonstration video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B27-cHMnlPE&t=17s). Two plates (45 lb + 25 lb, 31.75 kg total) rest on the shared lower loading arm coupled by a single taut flat belt to the upper shaped cam (CAM2). The handle yoke pivots freely on the rigid cam-arm mounting pin (R = 200.4 px about the cam axle) and acts as a two-force link along mount -> hand (pull_toward), giving the exact cam moment arm r_mount * sin(alpha) and exact elbow moment arm to the handle force line; force represents combined handle force across both hands.

observation.evidence: Five level near-side frames (frames 2-6 at 4 fps from t=17.0s, cropped 1080x1080 and resized to 1000x1000) from Hammer Strength's official Plate-Loaded Seated Biceps (PL-BI) demonstration video. The added plates (45 lb + 25 lb = 31.75 kg on the single shared lower loading horn) are marked at their mass-weighted center of mass along the loading sleeve (64.3% 45 lb, 35.7% 25 lb) rotating around the fixed lower bearing (pivot, near [530, 621]). A single taut flat belt connects the visible lower-arm clevis bolt (belt_load, radius 246-253 px from pivot) upward along the measured centerline between the two bright belt edges to the upper shaped cam (belt_cam), which rotates around the upper cam axle (cam_pivot, near [452, 357], verified to <1.4 px residual by circular-arc fit to the rigid cam-arm handle mount). Because the handle yoke pivots freely on the rigid cam-arm mounting pin (grip, R = 200.4 +/- 1.4 px about cam_pivot), it behaves as a two-force link transmitting force along mount -> hand (pull_toward). The exact cam moment arm is moment_arm(cam_pivot, mount, hand) = r_mount * sin(alpha) (178-201 px, with alpha = 63-88 deg), giving combined handle force 0.84 -> 0.86 -> 0.81 -> 0.73 -> 0.67 kgf/kg (forearm-tangential component 0.79 -> 0.83 -> 0.80 -> 0.73 -> 0.66 kgf/kg, matching direct conservation of work at the hand 0.76-0.84 kgf/kg and kinematic d(theta_load)/d(theta_cam) within 1-4%). The lifter's elbow joint center (near [529, 358]) is constrained to <0.7 px residual by circular-arc fits to both the hand (R = 256.5 px) and handle cap (R = 277.6 px), yielding 53.5-133.6 deg elbow flexion and exact elbow moment arm distance from the elbow to the mount -> hand force line (0.39-0.42 m using the 25 lb plate 0.343 m reference, cross-checked against the 45 lb 0.450 m plate in poses 1-3; ~7-10% near-side arm-plane perspective uncertainty).

motion_check.source: Hammer Strength Plate Loaded Seated Biceps demonstration, 1920 × 1080. Near-side view of a single lifting stroke. Original frames have no analysis overlays.
motion_check.extraction: Seek to 17.00 s, apply ffmpeg fps=4 for 5.8 s, use output frames 2–6 (1-based). Crop x=499, y=0, width=1080, height=1080 and resize to 1000 × 1000. Coordinates use top-left origin and y down.
motion_check.landmarks: anchor = near-side load-arm bearing cap. plates = estimated added-mass center between two plates. hand = estimated grip contact hidden by the hand. handle_cap = visible rigid end of the handle. rocker_pin = visible silver pin on the cam rocker.
motion_check.uncertainty: Anchor ±2 px, plate center approximately ±5 to 10 px, hand contact ±8 to 10 px, handle cap ±3 px. This calculation assumes a level, nearly side-on camera and comparable image scales at the hand and plates. The bearing corrects image translation. Parallax, rotating grips, unknown plate mass sharing and the chord approximation affect the result. The handle cap provides a sensitivity check. The rocker pin and grip cap sweep about different apparent centers. The work estimate follows the contact path directly because using grip radius about the cam axle would assume a rigid grip attachment.

base_resistance.source: Hammer Strength PL-BI placard and specification list 4 lb (1.8 kg) starting resistance for the shared workarm (0.9 kg per arm bilaterally). Held constant across the stroke because the unloaded arm curve is unreported.
